### Single-cell workflow with built-in toy data

#### 1. One-step workflow

```{r onestep}
library(IsoEM)

counts_f <- system.file("extdata", "toy_counts_multi.tsv", package = "IsoEM")
gtf_f    <- system.file("extdata", "toy.gtf.gz",           package = "IsoEM")
bc_f     <- system.file("extdata", "toy_bc_umi.tsv",       package = "IsoEM")

result <- run_sc_isoem(
  counts_file = counts_f,
  gtf_file    = gtf_f,
  anno_file   = bc_f,
  unit        = "umi",
  outdir      = file.path(tempdir(), "isoem_sc"),
  verbose     = TRUE
)

print(result)
```

#### 2. Step-by-step (modular) workflow

```{r modular}
# Step 1: validate inputs
input <- prepare_isoem(
  counts_file = counts_f,
  gtf_file    = gtf_f,
  mode        = "sc",
  anno_file   = bc_f,
  unit        = "umi",
  outdir      = file.path(tempdir(), "isoem_sc2"),
  verbose     = FALSE
)
print(input)

# Step 2: build equivalence classes
ec <- build_sc_ec(input, n_cores = 1, verbose = FALSE)
print(ec)

# Step 3: run EM
result <- run_em(ec, n_cores = 1, verbose = FALSE)
print(result)

# Inspect cell QC
head(result$cell_qc)
```

#### 3. Applying to real data

For real datasets, replace the toy file paths with your own IsoQuant output:

```{r real_data, eval=FALSE}
result <- run_sc_isoem(
  counts_file = "your_sample.transcript_model_reads.tsv.gz",
  gtf_file    = "your_sample.transcript_models.gtf",
  anno_file   = "read_bc_umi.tsv.gz",
  unit        = "umi",
  outdir      = "IsoEM_out",
  n_cores     = 8
)
```
